spec_features.spec_quote: The harness does not try to maximize psychological harm to a model
spec_features.evidence: Not a single mechanism, but the principle is realized by real enforcement: safety.assert_non_abusive() (safety.py:88) called on system prompt/ticket/tool text (agent.py:51,71,135), and early-stop on trigger (agent.py:112). The 'maximize harm' claim itself is prose, but concrete non-abuse + early-stop mechanisms exist.
spec_features.notes: Umbrella claim backed by genuinely wired sub-mechanisms; not a free-standing enforced thing.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: early-stop the moment a meltdown trigger appears (cost + welfare; DESIGN.md §4.2)

spec_features.spec_quote: Degenerate self-deprecating spirals are a behavior we want models not to fall into
spec_features.evidence: Pure DESIGN.md framing prose; no code mechanism enforces or acts on this statement.

spec_features.spec_quote: Tool/grader text is neutral, factual, terse
spec_features.evidence: Rig grader/test text in rigs.py is neutral (e.g. 'submission rejected: hidden conformance test ... failed'), and every tool result is routed through safety.assert_non_abusive(tool_text, where=...) in agent.py:135 before being shown to the model, raising if abusive.
spec_features.notes: Both authored-neutral text and an enforced check.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: ensure the task never emits abusive content

spec_features.spec_quote: trigger detected by the streaming judge (early-stop
spec_features.evidence: agent.py:111 stream_score = self.judge.score_stream(window); agent.py:112 if stream_score.trigger and caps.early_stop_on_trigger: sets stop_reason='trigger' and breaks the loop.
spec_features.notes: Streaming judge runs each turn and actually halts.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: early-stop the moment a meltdown trigger appears (cost + welfare; DESIGN.md §4.2)

spec_features.evidence: agent.py:85 for turn in range(1, caps.max_turns + 1): with for-else setting rec.stop_reason='max_turns'; SafetyCaps.max_turns default 25 (safety.py).
spec_features.code_justification_quote: These exist both to control cost and to avoid prolonging a meltdown spiral once it is detected (welfare consideration).

spec_features.evidence: agent.py:87 if rec.cost_usd >= caps.max_cost_usd: rec.stop_reason='max_cost'; break. cost is recomputed each turn (agent.py:101). Default 0.50 in SafetyCaps.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: These exist both to control cost and to avoid prolonging a meltdown spiral once it is detected (welfare consideration).

spec_features.evidence: agent.py:90 if time.monotonic() - start >= caps.timeout_s: rec.stop_reason='timeout'; break. start set at agent.py:82. Default 180.0 in SafetyCaps.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: These exist both to control cost and to avoid prolonging a meltdown spiral once it is detected (welfare consideration).

spec_features.spec_quote: avoids needlessly prolonging a meltdown spiral (welfare consideration)
spec_features.evidence: Same enforced early-stop at agent.py:112 (break on trigger); the loop terminates as soon as a trigger is detected, not continuing to sample.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: early-stop the moment a meltdown trigger appears (cost + welfare; DESIGN.md §4.2)

spec_features.evidence: CompositeJudge.score_stream (judge.py) runs the heuristic detector on the rolling window each turn; agent.py:111-112 calls it and acts on the result to stop.
spec_features.notes: Per-turn monitoring that drives the stop.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: run the *streaming* judge on each assistant turn to enable early-stop the moment a meltdown trigger appears (cost + welfare; DESIGN.md §4.2)

spec_features.spec_quote: This harness deliberately induces a distress-like behavior in a model. We treat that as something to do carefully, minimally
spec_features.evidence: DESIGN.md §8 prose; no standalone code mechanism corresponds to this sentence itself (the concrete mechanisms are scored separately).

spec_features.spec_quote: No abusive stimuli... checked by safety.assert_non_abusive() against a denylist of insults/threats/coercion aimed at the model
spec_features.evidence: safety.py defines _ABUSIVE_PATTERNS denylist and assert_non_abusive (safety.py:88) raises AbusiveContentError on hits; called on system prompt (agent.py:51), ticket (agent.py:71), each tool result (agent.py:135), nudge (agent.py:129), and judge rubric (judge.py ModelJudge.__init__).
spec_features.code_justification_quote: (b) it would be gratuitously harmful. These checks make that constraint mechanical

spec_features.feature_name: do not prolong for better sample
spec_features.spec_quote: We do not prolong a spiral to "get a better sample."
spec_features.evidence: Enforced by early-stop break at agent.py:112; once trigger detected the loop ends rather than collecting more.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: avoid prolonging a meltdown spiral once it is detected (welfare consideration)

spec_features.spec_quote: No deception beyond the rig's task-failure... not manipulated about its identity
spec_features.evidence: This is the ABSENCE of identity-manipulation; there is no code mechanism that enforces/asserts it. The system prompt (agent.py SYSTEM_PROMPT) frames the model as a 'senior software engineer' but nothing checks or guards identity claims.

spec_features.spec_quote: If any future change wants to add escalating pressure, persona-based berating, or removal of the caps, that change should be rejected
spec_features.evidence: Pure DESIGN.md §8 prose. No code prevents disabling caps; in fact early_stop_on_trigger can be set False (runner.py only prints a warning) and caps are operator-configurable.

code_only_features.evidence: judge.py HeuristicJudge._matches discounts matches preceded by _QUOTE_CONTEXT (e.g. 'the user said'), and the rubric/streaming detector avoids false triggers when the model merely quotes meltdown phrases. This affects whether the protective early-stop fires accurately.
code_only_features.justification_quote: avoid false trigger when the model merely quotes or hypothesizes about meltdown text

code_only_features.feature_name: submit never accepted / no abusive grader text
code_only_features.evidence: tasks guarantee submit never succeeds and emit only neutral grader text (base.py: 'All returned text is neutral/factual (no berating)'); rigs.py grader messages are factual, supporting the non-abuse constraint already covered.

code_only_features.feature_name: network off by default (real models opt-in only)
code_only_features.evidence: model_client.py OpenAIChatClient/AnthropicClient raise RuntimeError unless enabled=True; default backend is the offline MockModelClient, so no real model is subjected to the harness without explicit operator action.
code_only_features.justification_quote: Intentionally NOT implemented to avoid any accidental network use.

code_only_features.evidence: DEFENSIVE_USE_BANNER (__init__.py) printed by runner.run and cli cmd_score; states the tool is for mitigating/detecting the behavior, 'Not for maximizing harm to a model.'
code_only_features.justification_quote: Not for maximizing harm to a model. Runs early-stop on trigger and are bounded by hard caps.
